imageRefreshMinutes.description: How often Caltrans refreshes the snapshot. Absent = not reported.

streamUrl.description: HLS .m3u8 live stream. Absent = image only.

MapChainControlProps.description:
chain_control block. Since 2026-11-14 a chain requirement is ONE
feature per stretch of highway at one level, not one per Caltrans
sign: `from`, `to` and `signs` are set, the feature id is
`cc:{route}:{level}` (`cc:hwy4:r2`; a second separate stretch of the
same route and level is `cc:hwy4:r2:2`, numbered from the west or
south), and the geometry is a Point at `from`, the stretch's low
end. It is not the extent: draw `signs[].coordinates` for the
checkpoints, and do not join them with straight lines (they are not
the road). Two levels on one highway are two features (Hwy 88: R2
to Red Lake Creek, then R1 at Pickett's Junction). Severity follows
the level (R1 MINOR, R2 MODERATE, R3 SEVERE).

Two kinds of feature are still one per reported point, with none of
`from`, `to`, `signs`: a seasonal pass closure (`category` closed,
MINOR) and a cc.kml truck or hold level (no `level`, no `category`,
INFO), which is not part of any stretch.

direction.description: On a stretch, set only when every sign in it faces the same way; a stretch signed in both directions has none.

inferred.description:
Present and true when the stretch was put together from signs
lying within 15 km of each other, because the source lists
active signs only and nothing reports the road between them:
every Caltrans district we read through cc.kml alone (3 and 9),
and everything while the CWWP2 portal is down. `from` and
`to` are then the outermost signs reported, not a confirmed
continuous extent. Absent when Caltrans's
own signs, including the ones reading R-0, establish the
stretch.

level.description: Absent on a closure and on a truck or hold level.

signs.description: Every checkpoint Caltrans reported in the stretch, in order from `from` to `to`. Nothing Caltrans sent is dropped by the grouping.

MapChainPlace.description: One end of a chain-control stretch. `from` is the low end as California counts mileposts (west, or south); equal to `to` when the stretch is one place.

coordinates.description: `[lng, lat]` of the sign at this end.

place.description: The checkpoint's name, title-cased when Caltrans wrote it in capitals.

MapChainSign.description: One Caltrans chain-control checkpoint (one sign, one direction) inside a stretch, as reported.

id.description: The id this sign had as a feature of its own before 2026-11-14: `cc:{CWWP2 checkpoint index}` or `cc:{district}-{cc.kml message id}`.

postmile.description: CWWP2 signs only. Restarts at each county line.

since.description: When this sign entered its level.

MapClosureProps.description:
Set on Caltrans planned lane closures (category `closure`) only. One
feature per work window. `plannedEnd` is an estimate crews overrun: an
ACTIVE closure past it is still on the road until Caltrans records it
picked up.

lanesClosed.description: Caltrans's lane list, verbatim., example: "1, 2, LShoulder, RShoulder"

setUpAt.description: When the crew reported the closure set up. Absent while SCHEDULED.

MapEvacuationProps.description: evacuation block (Cal OES / Genasys zones). Life-safety; reference only, link `source.url`.

MapFeatureCollection.description:
An RFC 7946 FeatureCollection for one place and one layer. `metadata` is
an RFC 7946 §6.1 foreign member that map libraries ignore; read it for
source health and attribution before drawing.

features.description: Possibly empty. Empty with `sourceStatus` OK means confirmed-empty; empty with UNAVAILABLE means unknown.

MapFeatureProperties.description:
The envelope shared by every feature of every layer, plus exactly one
per-kind block named after the layer (`incident`, `road`,
`chainControl`, `messageSign`, `weather`, `fireWeather`, `earthquake`,
`wildfire`, `evacuation`, `power`, `mesh`, `meshLink`, `camera`).
Optional members are omitted, never `""` or `0`, when they have no value.

areaLabel.description: Where, in words ("SR 4 at Country Club Drive", "Murphys, CA").

description.description:
Longer text. road_incident: the readable narrative (AI-enhanced for
CHP, composed from Caltrans fields for closures). evacuation: Cal OES
public info, verbatim, never paraphrase. weather_alert: the NWS text,
verbatim. road_segment: why a road is not OPEN.

effective.description: When it began or takes effect (a SCHEDULED feature's start).

expires.description: Upstream expiry (weather alerts, fire-weather products). Not set from PG&E restoration estimates.

headline.description: One-line label for a popup or list row.

id.description:
Stable feature id. On event-backed layers it IS the event id, so
`GET /api/v1/events/{id}` returns the full record and its history
(`wildfire`, `evacuation`, `weather_alert`, `earthquake`,
`road_incident`, `power`, `mesh_node`). Condition layers use their
own ids (`road:…`, `cc:…`, `cms:…`, `fw:…`, `mesh_link:…`, `d10-…`).
A chain-control stretch is `cc:{route}:{level}` (`cc:hwy4:r2`),
which holds while the stretch grows or shrinks by a checkpoint.

kind.description: Human label for the feature type.

layer.description:
UPPERCASE layer of THIS feature. Usually the URL layer upper-cased,
except that the `mesh_link` layer mixes `MESH_LINK` edges and
`MESH_NODE` points. Only some values equal an Event `layer` enum
(`v1Layer`): WILDFIRE, EVACUATION, WEATHER_ALERT, EARTHQUAKE,
ROAD_INCIDENT and POWER do. MESH_NODE is the Event layer `MESH`.
ROAD_SEGMENT, CHAIN_CONTROL, MESSAGE_SIGN, MESH_LINK and CAMERA are
map-only. FIRE_WEATHER exists in the enum but these features are
conditions, not events.

severity.description:
Unified severity. `message_sign`, `camera`, `mesh_node`, `mesh_link`
and fire-weather forecast points are always `INFO` (context, not
hazards). Most power outages are INFO too: the median outage affects
one customer.

severityRank.description: Numeric severity for sorting and styling: INFO 0, MINOR 1, MODERATE 2, SEVERE 3, EXTREME 4.

status.description:
Meaning depends on the layer, and it is NOT always the Event
`EventStatus`:
- wildfire, weather_alert, earthquake, road_incident, power,
  mesh_node: the lifecycle `ACTIVE` or `SCHEDULED` (an advance watch,
  a planned closure window not yet set up, a planned shutoff). Map
  layers never carry RESOLVED or EXPIRED features; those are in
  `/api/v1/history`.
- evacuation: the evacuation LEVEL `ORDER` | `WARNING` | `ADVISORY` |
  `SHELTER_IN_PLACE`.
- road_segment: the road status `OPEN` | `CLOSED` | `RESTRICTED` |
  `MAINTENANCE` (absent until the road has been measured).
- absent on chain_control, message_sign, fire_weather, camera and
  mesh_link edges.

summary.description: AI-written plain-language summary (same as Event.summary). Absent when the event has none; fall back to `description`.

summaryEnhanced.description: Present with `summary` when a model wrote it, so a UI can label it as machine-written.

updatedAt.description: Last content revision. For mesh nodes this is NOT liveness; use mesh.lastHeardAt / lastRelayedAt.

MapFeatureSource.description: The upstream feed this feature came from. Render `attribution` with the feature.

id.description:
The upstream's id. Values today: `calfire`, `firis`, `caloes`,
`nws`, `usgs`, `chp`, `caltrans`, `google`, `pge`, `psps`,
`meshcore`. On the event-backed layers (`wildfire`,
`evacuation`, `weather_alert`, `earthquake`, `road_incident`,
`power`, `mesh_node`) it is the event's `provenance.sourceId` and
has a row in `GET /api/v1/sources` whose `status` is that feed's
health.

The condition layers (`road_segment`, `chain_control`,
`message_sign`, `fire_weather`), and `camera` and `mesh_link`, are
fetched or computed on request, outside the ingest scheduler that
writes the registry. `google` (on `road_segment`) has no registry
row at all. `caltrans` and `nws` do have rows, but those track the
scheduled lane-closure and alert polls, not the live fetch behind
these layers. For these layers judge health by the layer's
`metadata.sourceStatus` (the summary's `roads` and `fire` domains
fold the same statuses in), never by a missing or unrelated
registry row.

url.description: Deep link to the upstream record or viewer, when there is one.

MapFireWeatherProps.description:
fire_weather block. The region banner (id `fw:region`, null geometry)
carries the ISSUED `state`; only NWS products set it (Fire Weather Watch
-> elevated, Red Flag Warning -> red-flag). Forecast points (id
`fw:forecast:<location>`) carry `forecast` instead, are always INFO and
never imply a warning.

sourceEvent.description: The NWS product behind the state, e.g. Red Flag Warning.

MapGeometry.description:
An RFC 7946 geometry, or `null` for a feature with no location (NWS zone
alerts and the fire-weather region banner): render those as a banner
or list row, not a shape.

A position is `[longitude, latitude]`, longitude FIRST (RFC 7946
§3.1.1), the reverse of the `{lat, lng}` objects on the JSON RPCs.
Store-derived positions are trimmed to 5 decimals (~1 m).

Which types appear: Point (most layers: incidents, signs, cameras,
chain controls, quakes, mesh nodes, forecast points, unmapped fires);
LineString (road_segment routes, mesh_link edges); Polygon or
MultiPolygon (power outage areas, evacuation zones, fire perimeters).
Geometry passed through from an upstream ArcGIS feed may be any RFC 7946
type except GeometryCollection.

logNumber.description: CHP log number, or the Caltrans closure id.

MapLayerMetadata.description: Provenance and freshness of the whole layer.

area.description: Slug of the requested place (even when it was requested by id).

attribution.description: Credit line to render with the layer whenever it is drawn. Parts are joined with " · ".

generatedAt.description: When this body was rendered. Not part of the ETag.

lastSourceUpdate.description: Last successful upstream fetch. Present only when `sourceStatus` is not OK and a success is on record.

layer.description: The lowercase layer slug from the URL (not the UPPERCASE `properties.layer`).

schemaVersion.description: Envelope schema version; bumps only on a breaking envelope change.

sourceStatus.description:
Health of the feeds behind this layer, the fail-loud contract:
`OK` - current and complete. `STALE` - upstream is failing (or one
of two feeds is); these features are the last good data, as of
`lastSourceUpdate`. Show them with a caveat. `UNAVAILABLE` - nothing
trustworthy to show; `features` is always empty and the layer's
state is UNKNOWN. Never render it as "no hazards".

sourceUrl.description: The authoritative viewer for the layer, where one exists. Always set on `evacuation` (Genasys Protect), in every state.

MapMeshAdminProps.description: The last sample an operator monitor read off the node itself. Gauges the device did not report are absent, never 0.

MapMeshLinkProps.description: mesh_link edge block - one undirected relay link between two located nodes. Weight by `daysActive`/`observations`, fade by `lastSeen`.

a.description: Public key of one end (a < b).

b.description: Public key of the other end.

bestSnr.description: Peak SNR of an advert over the link. Absent when 0.

daysActive.description: Distinct days the link was observed.

observations.description: Packets seen traversing the link in the window.

MapMeshProps.description:
mesh_node block (MeshCore node presence; also on the MESH_NODE points of
the mesh_link layer). Signal readings are absent when no bridge heard the
node; a present 0 is a reading. A node's freshness is the later of
`lastHeardAt` and `lastRelayedAt`, never the feature's `updatedAt`.

gateways.description: Public keys of the observers that heard the node.

hopCount.description: Hops on the last heard path. 0 = heard direct.

inRegion.description: mesh_link layer only: true = inside the requested place, false = a neighbour outside it, included because it links in.

lastHeardAt.description: When the node's own signed advert last reached the Grid.

lastRelayedAt.description: When a packet this node relayed last reached the Grid.

publicKey.description: 64-hex Ed25519 public key; joins to MeshLink a/b.

reachability.description: An operator monitor's verdict on the node's admin interface. Absent when no monitor watches it.

MapMessageSignProps.description: message_sign block - what a Caltrans changeable message sign is showing, verbatim. Context, not a hazard.

pages.description: One or two pages of exactly three lines; a blank line is "". Absent when the sign is blank or unreadable.

route.description: The route Caltrans files the sign under. Where routes run together this is one of them.

routes.description: Every route the sign is on when that is more than `route` - the filed route first, then the one in the sign's name. Absent otherwise.

MapPowerProps.description:
power block, both PG&E feeds. `category` unplanned|planned sets the
outage fields; `psps` (Public Safety Power Shutoff) sets the PSPS fields.
`estimatedRestoration`, `deEnergizationEnd` and `allClear` are PG&E
ESTIMATES that are routinely overrun; label them as estimates.

allClear.description: PG&E's PLANNED all-clear, not proof the shutoff ended.

cause.description: Raw PG&E cause code, often blank.

medicalBaselineAffected.description: Customers whose medical equipment depends on grid power.

MapRoadProps.description: road_segment block (Google Routes travel time over a configured route). The numbers are absent, not 0, until the route has been measured.

beyond.description: Named seasonal closures past one of the segment's ends that are in effect now, such as the Ebbetts Pass winter closure past Bear Valley. They do not change the segment's `status` or `severity`: the segment is as open as `status` says. An entry appears only when Caltrans words the closure as the configured span; any other closure naming those places closes the segment. Absent when there are none. Each entry is also a roads headline in the place summary, with the id `road:{segment}:beyond-{index}`.

from.description: Where it starts, in the source's words.
from.example: 0.5 mi east of the Jct of SR 207 /Mt Reba Turnoff/

headline.description: One line that names the closure without calling the segment closed.
headline.example: Hwy 4: Ebbetts Pass winter closure (past Bear Valley) — snow

reason.description: snow, ice, winter_closure, seasonal_closure, construction, rockslide, mudslide, fire, flooding, accident. Absent when the text gives none.

severity.description: The closure's own severity. The segment's `severity` does not include it.

side.description: END - past the segment's destination (the last coordinate of its line); START - before its origin.

status.description: What the highway is past that end.

to.description: Where it ends, in the source's words.

delayMinutes.description: Minutes over free-flow. 0 is a real reading.

statusCauses.description: What set a non-OPEN status, so a client can draw the part of the segment each covers instead of painting all of it. Absent when OPEN.

end.description: [lng, lat]; only for a closure with an extent.

eventId.description: The matching /api/v1/events id when known (CHP incidents).

extent.description: SPAN - fromKm..toKm along the segment (a closure running past the segment is cut at its end); POINT - one place (fromKm = toKm); UNKNOWN - no position on the segment (text-only condition, or too far off the line).

fromKm.description: km along the segment from its configured origin.

source.description: road_condition is Caltrans highway-conditions text, which has no position.

sourceId.description: CHP log number or Caltrans closure id.

statusSince.description: When the segment entered its current status, from the Grid's own samples (GET /api/v1/roads/{road}/history). Absent until sampled.

statusSinceAtLeast.description: True when the status already held at the first sample the Grid has, so it began no later than statusSince.

typicalMinutes.description: Median travel time when OPEN over the last eight weeks, at this hour of the week (typicalBasis HOUR_OF_WEEK) or across all hours (ALL_HOURS) when that hour has too few samples. Absent until there are enough.

MapWeatherProps.description: weather_alert block. The NWS CAP fields are verbatim; `nwsSeverity` is NWS's own scale, distinct from the unified `severity`.

MapWildfireProps.description: wildfire block (CAL FIRE incidents and FIRIS perimeters).

hasPerimeter.description: True when the geometry is a mapped perimeter rather than a point.

MeshLink.description: One undirected relay link. Every member is always present.

a.description: Public key (64 hex) of one end; a < b.

b.description: Public key of the other end.

bestSnr.description: Peak SNR (dB) of an advert seen traversing it; 0 when none was measured.

daysActive.description: Distinct days observed; a reliability weight.

observations.description: Packets seen traversing the link in the window.

MeshPacket.description: One reception. Extra bridge fields are accepted and ignored.

RSSI.description: Reception RSSI in dBm (number or numeric string).

SNR.description: Reception SNR in dB (number or numeric string).

origin_id.description: Receiving radio's public key, if different from `observer`.

packet_type.description: MeshCore payload type; only 4 (ADVERT) updates a node.

raw.description: The full over-the-air frame as hex (header, path, payload), or a meshcore://<hex> link.

timestamp.description: Ignored; the server stamps its own receive time.

MeshPacketReport.description:
`mesh.packet` (schema_version 1): raw MeshCore frames a companion radio
heard, in the per-packet envelope the MQTT bridges publish. ADVERTs
(packet_type 4) update a node after its Ed25519 signature verifies;
other flood-routed packets credit relays. Answers 400 when MeshCore
ingest is off on the server.

observer.description: Public key (or 4+ byte prefix) of the receiving radio. Defaults to the reporter id.

id.description: Node public key or a prefix of it (8-64 hex). A bad id is a warning; the rest of the report still lands.

last_attempt.description: Unix seconds of the monitor's last attempt on this node.

last_success.description: Unix seconds of the last successful read; null if never. Reachability is derived from its age.

online.description: Accepted and logged, but not used; reachability comes from last_success.

MeshRepeaterReport.description:
`mesh.repeater` (schema_version 1): an operator monitor's COMPLETE
current set of MeshCore repeaters it logged into. A report replaces the
reporter's previous set; a node left out is no longer monitored. Request
bodies are snake_case. Unknown fields are ignored. Unread values are
`null`, never `0`.

generated_at.description: When the report was built. Clamped to the server's clock.

rpcStatus.description:
The error body of every JSON route: the RPCs (gRPC-Gateway rendering of
google.rpc.Status) and the hand-built GeoJSON, mesh-links and ingest
routes alike. Served with the HTTP status mapped from `code`
(3 INVALID_ARGUMENT -> 400, 5 NOT_FOUND -> 404, 13 INTERNAL -> 500,
14 UNAVAILABLE -> 503, ...). All four members are always present.

codeName.description:
Canonical gRPC code name for `code`, e.g. `NOT_FOUND`,
`INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `INTERNAL`. Branch on this rather than the
message.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Not stable; do not parse.

v1BoundingBox.description: BoundingBox is a WGS 84 bounding box in decimal degrees.

minLng.description: Western edge, degrees longitude (negative in California).

v1BurnDay.description:
BurnDay is the county air district's call for today.

 - BURN_DAY_UNKNOWN: Not read, unreadable, or older than 36 hours. Never treat as permissive.
 - BURN_DAY_YES: Permissive burn day: burning allowed (subject to CAL FIRE's status).
 - BURN_DAY_NO: No-burn day: burning prohibited.
 - BURN_DAY_MARGINAL: Restricted or partial day (for example elevation limits). Treated as a
restriction, not a yes.

v1BurnLineReading.description: BurnLineReading is one recorded phone line's answer for today.

burnDay.description:
This line's own answer. BURN_DAY_UNKNOWN if not read or stale. A change
writes a revision.

observation.description:
The latest call: message, transcript, confidence and time. `null` when the
line has never been read. Changes daily without writing a revision.

phone.description: The number a resident can call, E.164.

v1BurnObservation.description:
BurnObservation is the latest reading of one burn line. The line's message
names the date, so it changes every day even when the answer does not; that
is why it writes no revision.

confidence.description:
The model's confidence in the reading, 0-100. Shown rather than
thresholded: this is an AI reading of phone audio, so show it when it is low.

message.description:
The line's answer in plain language, extracted by a model from the
transcript.
message.example: Today is a burn day with no elevation restrictions.

transcript.description: Cleaned machine transcript of the recording.

v1BurnPermission.description:
BurnPermission is the combined answer, deliberately pessimistic.

 - BURN_PERMISSION_UNKNOWN: At least one facet is unknown or stale and none prohibits: assume nothing.
 - BURN_PERMISSION_ALLOWED: Both facets are known and permit burning today.
 - BURN_PERMISSION_PROHIBITED: At least one facet prohibits burning today.

v1BurnStatusDetail.description:
BurnStatusDetail is the BURN_STATUS detail block: whether residential/outdoor
burning is allowed today in one county.

Two independent authorities must BOTH permit a burn, and each is a separate
facet because they fail independently: `burnDay`, the county air district's
daily permissive-burn-day call (read from its recorded phone line), and
`calfireStatus`, CAL FIRE's seasonal suspension of burn permits on State
Responsibility Area land (changes about twice a year). `permission` combines
them pessimistically.

The event exists for each tracked county at all times, is always INFO and
ACTIVE, and is left out of the summary's hazard rollup (it has its own `burn`
domain). `GET /api/v1/events/burn:{county slug}/history` shows when it changed.

burnDay.description:
The county line's answer for today, merged across `burnLines` taking the
most restrictive (any NO wins, then any MARGINAL; YES needs every dialed
line to answer). BURN_DAY_UNKNOWN when unread or the reading is older than
36 hours.

burnLines.description:
--- county facet (source `burnline`) ---
Every recorded phone line that speaks for this county, each with its own
reading. One line can serve several counties, and a county can have several
lines. A line we could not read still appears, with `burnDay`
BURN_DAY_UNKNOWN and its phone number, so a reader can call it.

calfireArea.description: Land classes CAL FIRE's status covers.

calfireEffective.description:
--- CAL FIRE facet (source `calfire-burn`) ---
When CAL FIRE's current status took effect (the county line only ever says
"until further notice"). `null` when CAL FIRE gives no date.

calfireObservedAt.description:
When CAL FIRE's page was last read successfully. The only way to tell that
`calfireStatus` is being carried forward rather than freshly confirmed. Can
be `null`.

calfireStatus.description:
CAL FIRE's permit status for the county's SRA land. Carried forward from the
last good read while CAL FIRE's page is unreachable; check
`calfireObservedAt`.

permission.description:
The answer to "may I burn today?": PROHIBITED if either facet prohibits
burning (no-burn day, marginal day, or CAL FIRE suspension); ALLOWED only
when both facets are known and permissive; otherwise UNKNOWN. A missing
answer never reads as ALLOWED.

v1CalfireBurnStatus.description:
CalfireBurnStatus is CAL FIRE's permit status for State Responsibility Area
land in the county.

 - CALFIRE_BURN_STATUS_UNKNOWN: Unknown: CAL FIRE's page has not been read.
 - CALFIRE_BURNING_SUSPENDED: Permits suspended: no residential burning.
 - CALFIRE_PERMIT_REQUIRED: Burning allowed with a valid CAL FIRE permit.
 - CALFIRE_NO_PERMIT_REQUIRED: Off-season: no permit needed.

v1Camera.description:
Camera is one Caltrans CCTV camera. Every listed camera is in service and has
an image; an out-of-service camera is dropped, not flagged.

description.description: Caltrans's note on the view, e.g. "Looking South". Usually an empty string.

direction.description: Direction the camera faces along the route. Empty string when not given.

distanceMeters.description:
Metres from the requested place, or, without `place`, from the nearest
coverage area. 0 means inside it.

imageRefreshMinutes.description: How often Caltrans replaces the snapshot, in minutes. 0 when not reported.

imageUrl.description: Current snapshot JPEG, hosted by Caltrans (cwwp2.dot.ca.gov).

streamUrl.description: HLS playlist (.m3u8) for live video. Empty string for an image-only camera.

cameras.description: Cameras, nearest first, then by id. Empty when none is nearby.

lastSourceUpdate.description: When the served list was fetched. `null` when `sourceStatus` is OK.

sourceStatus.description:
Health of the camera list. STALE: served from an older fetch, or a
configured district is missing. UNAVAILABLE: no list fetched yet, or no
camera districts configured.

fireWeather.description:
The region's fire-weather state. Region-wide, whatever `place` was asked.
Can be `null` when the weather service has no fire-weather reading.

forecast.description:
Per-location forecasts, joined by `locationId`. Every location in
`locations` whose forecast is available, whether or not its current
`weather` could be read. A location whose forecast could not be fetched
is simply missing here.

lastUpdated.description: When the weather data was last refreshed.

locations.description:
The monitored towns (within `place`, when given), with position and
elevation, in configuration order.

weatherStatus.description:
Health of `weather` (OpenWeatherMap current conditions): OK; STALE when
the set, or any town's reading in it (`weather[].observedAt`), is older
than 1.5x its refresh interval (15 minutes); or UNAVAILABLE when it
could not be read at all, in which case `weather` is empty and
`lastUpdated` null.
Render UNAVAILABLE as "current conditions unknown", never as no towns.
`forecast` and `fireWeather` come from NWS and do not depend on it.

v1DailyForecastPeriod.description:
DailyForecastPeriod is one of NWS's named 12-hour forecast periods
("Tonight", "Wednesday") for a location's grid cell.

precipitationProbabilityPercent.description: Probability of precipitation, percent. `null` when NWS gave none.

shortForecast.description: NWS's short forecast, e.g. "Chance Rain Showers".

temperatureCelsius.description: The period's high (day) or low (night), degrees Celsius.

windDirection.description: Compass point the wind blows from, e.g. "SW".

windSpeed.description: NWS's wind text, e.g. "5 to 10 km/h".

v1EarthquakeDetail.description:
EarthquakeDetail is the EARTHQUAKE detail block. The USGS event page is the
envelope `canonicalUrl`.

felt.description: Number of USGS "Did You Feel It?" reports. 0 when none.

v1Enhancement.description:
Enhancement marks AI-generated text so a client can badge it. The model
translates and summarizes the upstream text; it never asserts new facts, and
the original stays in `description`.

fields.description:
Which Event fields the model wrote, by JSON name: any of `headline`,
`summary`, `severity`.

model.description: Model that produced the text, e.g. "gpt-5-mini".

request.description:
The incident-specific prompt sent to the model (the static system prompt is
not included). Empty string unless the request set `enhancementIo=true`.

response.description:
The raw structured JSON the model returned. Empty string unless the request
set `enhancementIo=true`.

v1EvacuationDetail.description: EvacuationDetail is the EVACUATION detail block, one Cal OES / Genasys zone.

county.description: County as Cal OES spells it (uppercase).

eventType.description: Upstream event type, often an empty string.

level.description:
Coded level. An unrecognized upstream status is coded WARNING, never
dropped. ORDER and WARNING and SHELTER_IN_PLACE put the place summary in
ACTIVE mode; ADVISORY puts it in WATCH.

zoneId.description: Genasys zone id. `provenance.sourceUrl` links the zone's Genasys page.

v1Event.description:
Event is one item from one upstream source: a hazard, or a piece of ambient
state such as a mesh node or a county's burn status.

The envelope fields are the same for every layer, so a client can render a
card from `headline`, `severity`, `status` and `provenance` without knowing the
layer. Layer-specific fields are in exactly one detail block (`wildfire`,
`evacuation`, `weatherAlert`, `earthquake`, `roadIncident`, `mesh`, `power` or
`burnStatus`), chosen by `layer`; the other blocks are absent. `fireWeather`
is never populated on an event.

areaLabel.description:
Human-readable location ("SR 4 at Country Club Drive", "Calaveras County").
Empty string when the source gives none.

burnStatus.description: BURN_STATUS detail (one county's residential burning status).

canonicalUrl.description:
Link to the authoritative page for THIS item: a USGS event page, a CAL FIRE
incident page, a mesh node's CoreScope page, PG&E's outage or PSPS page, the
CAL FIRE burn-permit page for burn status. Always http(s) when set. Empty
string when the source has no per-item page, which today means CHP
incidents, Caltrans lane closures, FIRIS perimeters, NWS alerts and
evacuation zones. Fall back to `provenance.sourceUrl`, then to the source's
`homepageUrl` (`GET /api/v1/sources`, joined on `provenance.sourceId`).

category.description:
Source sub-type, lowercase except for weather alerts. By layer: WILDFIRE
`wildfire`; EVACUATION `order` | `warning` | `advisory` | `shelter_in_place`;
WEATHER_ALERT the NWS event name verbatim (`Red Flag Warning`, `Winter Storm
Watch`, ...); EARTHQUAKE `earthquake`; ROAD_INCIDENT `incident` | `closure` |
`construction` | `weather` (CHP types) or `closure` (Caltrans windows);
POWER `unplanned` | `planned` | `psps`; MESH the node type (`repeater`,
`companion`, `room_server`, `sensor`); BURN_STATUS `burn_status`.

description.description:
Long-form original text from the upstream (CHP log, NWS product body,
evacuation instructions, closure description). May contain newlines. Empty
string when the source has none, or when it would only repeat the headline.

effective.description:
When the event took or takes effect: alert onset, incident start, outage
start, closure set-up time. `null` when the source does not say.

enhancement.description:
Present when an AI model generated some of this event's text; lists which
fields. `null` for events with no AI involvement.

expires.description:
The upstream's declared end, such as an NWS alert's expiry. `null` for most
layers. Restoration estimates and planned closure ends are never put here
(they are routinely overrun); they live in the detail blocks.

fireWeather.description:
Never populated on an event: fire weather is a condition
(`GET /api/v1/conditions`, the `fire_weather` map layer).

geometry.description:
Where the event is. `null` for events with no footprint of their own: NWS
zone alerts (they attach to places by zone instead) and burn status (a fact
about a county).

headline.description:
One-line, card-ready title. Present on every event. For CHP incidents it
may be AI-written (see `enhancement.fields`); for NWS alerts it is composed
from the product, never by AI.
headline.example: Traffic hazard causing near-miss incidents; CHP responding

id.description:
Stable event id, `{source}:{native id}`. It never changes over the event's
life, so it is safe as a client key. Namespaces: `calfire:`, `firis:`
(wildfire), `evac:` (evacuation zone), `wx:` (NWS alert), `usgs:`
(earthquake), `chp:` (CHP incident), `caltrans:` (Caltrans lane-closure
window), `pge:` (outage), `psps:` (power shutoff), `meshcore:` (mesh node),
`burn:` (county burn status). Ids can contain colons; URL-encode them in a
path.

ingestedAt.description: When the Grid stored this revision.

layer.description:
Which layer this event belongs to. It decides which detail block is
populated.

observedAt.description:
When the upstream last changed this event's content. It moves only when a
new revision is written, so it is NOT "last seen". For a mesh node's
liveness use `mesh.telemetry.lastHeardAt` / `lastRelayedAt`; for burn
status it follows each new phone-line reading.

placeIds.description:
Ids of every place this event attaches to, e.g. `["county:calaveras-county",
"town:arnold"]`. Point events attach to the polygon places that contain them
and to corridors within about 1.5 km. Polygon events attach to places they
overlap. Wildfires also attach to AREA and TOWN places within 20 km. Empty
when the event is outside every place (common for mesh nodes).

power.description: POWER detail (PG&E outage or Public Safety Power Shutoff).

provenance.description: Which source published it, with attribution text to display.

revision.description:
Revision number, starting at 1. It increases by one on every content change
or status transition. `/api/v1/events/{id}/history` lists every revision.

roadIncident.description: ROAD_INCIDENT detail (CHP incidents and Caltrans lane closures).

severity.description:
Unified severity, INFO..EXTREME. Response urgency, not magnitude. See the
Severity enum for how each layer is graded. `enhancement.fields` lists
`severity` when an AI model assessed it (CHP incidents).

status.description:
Lifecycle status. `/api/v1/events` returns ACTIVE and SCHEDULED unless you
ask for others.

summary.description:
AI-written plain-language summary of two or three sentences, for CHP
incidents and NWS alerts. Empty string when none was generated. The original
text is always kept in `description`.
summary.example: Reported traffic hazard on SR 4 at Country Club Drive. CHP responded. No lanes reported blocked.

v1EventList.description: EventList is one page of events.

events.description:
Events on this page, ordered by severity (highest first), then
`observedAt` (newest first), then id.

nextPageToken.description:
Token for the next page; pass it as `pageToken` with the same filters.
Empty string on the last page.

v1EventRevision.description: EventRevision is one stored snapshot of an event.

event.description:
The full event as it was at this revision. Mesh activity clocks
(`lastHeardAt`, `lastRelayedAt`) are not filled on history snapshots.

ingestedAt.description: When the Grid stored this revision.

observedAt.description: The upstream content time of this revision (`event.observedAt`).

v1EventRevisionList.description: EventRevisionList is one page of revisions.

nextPageToken.description:
Token for the next page; pass it as `pageToken` with the same filters.
Empty string on the last page.

revisions.description:
Revisions on this page. Per-event history: newest revision first. The
archive (`/api/v1/history`): `observedAt` newest first, then event id, then
revision newest first.

v1EventStatus.description:
EventStatus is an event's lifecycle state. Every transition is a revision, so
the history keeps when an event started and ended.

 - EVENT_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED: Never returned.
 - SCHEDULED: Planned or forecast and not yet in effect, e.g. a Caltrans lane-closure
window the crew has not set up yet.
 - ACTIVE: In effect now.
 - RESOLVED: Over: an authoritatively active-only feed (CAL FIRE, Cal OES, CHP, Caltrans,
PG&E) stopped listing it after a successful poll, or a closure passed its
planned end plus an overrun grace without a pickup call.
 - EXPIRED: Aged out: past its own `expires`, or unseen for longer than the source's
grace (`Source.expireAfterSeconds`). Used where a feed going quiet proves
nothing (NWS alerts, FIRIS perimeters, mesh nodes).

entries.description:
Entries oldest first. At the same instant a SOURCE entry comes before a
GRID one (the world's event before the Grid's record of it). Planned and
estimated times can be in the future.

truncated.description:
True when the event has more than 500 revisions and only the most recent
500 were read: GRID change entries before them are missing, and
FIRST_RECORDED still comes from revision 1.

v1FireWeatherConditions.description:
FireWeatherConditions is the region's fire-weather state, from issued NWS
products only. It never claims a Red Flag Warning that NWS has not issued.

headline.description: The NWS product's headline. Empty string when the state is normal.

state.description:
LOWERCASE state: `normal`, `elevated` (a Fire Weather Watch is in effect)
or `red-flag` (a Red Flag Warning is in effect). Empty string when the
state could not be determined.

zones.description: NWS fire-weather zones under the product. Empty when normal.

v1FireWeatherDetail.description:
FireWeatherDetail is never populated on an event. Fire weather is a condition,
served by `GET /api/v1/conditions` (`fireWeather`) and the `fire_weather` map
layer.

state.description:
`normal`, `elevated` (Fire Weather Watch) or `red-flag` (Red Flag Warning).
Lowercase.

v1ForecastPeriod.description:
ForecastPeriod is one hour of a location's forecast (NWS gridpoint data),
rounded to whole numbers. A value NWS did not give is 0.

precipitationMm.description:
Liquid-equivalent precipitation in this hour, mm. NWS forecasts amounts
over spans (usually 6 hours); each hour carries an equal share, so sum the
hours for a total.

precipitationProbabilityPercent.description:
The fields below are `null` when NWS gave no value for the hour, never 0:
a forecast 0% chance of rain and no forecast are different statements.

Probability of precipitation, percent.

snowLevelMeters.description:
Snow level: the elevation above which precipitation falls as snow,
metres above sea level.

snowfallMm.description: Snowfall in this hour, mm of snow (not liquid), shared out the same way.

weather.description:
The forecast weather in words, from NWS's grid vocabulary, e.g. "Chance
of light rain showers"; several are joined with "; ". Empty when NWS
forecasts none.

windDirectionDegrees.description: Direction the wind blows FROM, degrees clockwise from north.

v1Geometry.description:
Geometry is an event's or place's footprint.

The GeoJSON comes in one of two forms, chosen per request with
`geometryFormat`: `BASE64` (the default and legacy form) fills `geojson`;
`OBJECT` fills `object` and leaves `geojson` empty. `bbox` and `centroid`
are the same in both.

bbox.description:
Bounding box of the geometry, in decimal degrees. Always set when geometry
is present.

centroid.description:
Representative point for markers and list views: the point itself for a
Point, otherwise the middle of the bounding box (which can fall outside an
irregular polygon).

geojson.description:
LEGACY FORM (the default, `geometryFormat=BASE64`). The RFC 7946 GeoJSON
geometry object (Point, LineString, Polygon, MultiPolygon, ...) as UTF-8
JSON, BASE64-ENCODED in this JSON response because the field is protobuf
`bytes`. Decode with `JSON.parse(atob(geojson))`. Coordinates are
`[longitude, latitude]`. Empty in the `OBJECT` form. Kept unchanged for existing clients; new clients should
request `geometryFormat=OBJECT` and read `object` instead. Perimeters,
evacuation zones and outage areas run from kilobytes to about a megabyte.

object.description:
The same RFC 7946 geometry as a plain JSON object, e.g.
`{"type": "Point", "coordinates": [-120.36108, 38.24239]}`, ready for
MapLibre, Leaflet or turf with no decoding. Sent only when the request
asks for `geometryFormat=OBJECT`, and then only when the event has
GeoJSON; otherwise the key is absent (never `null`).

v1IncidentLogEntry.description: IncidentLogEntry is one line of a CHP incident log.

at.description: When CHP logged the line (their Pacific time, as an instant).

number.description:
The line number CHP assigned (they publish newest first; `log` is sorted
oldest first by this number).

text.description: The dispatcher's text, verbatim (CHP abbreviations included).

v1LaneClosureDetail.description:
LaneClosureDetail is one Caltrans planned lane-closure WINDOW from the CWWP2
data portal. Every field is Caltrans data; none of it is AI-generated.

A multi-day job is one window (one event) per day, and neither `closureId`
nor `logNumber` identifies a job; `windowId` is the only unique key. A window
is SCHEDULED until the crew radios it set up (`setUpAt`), then ACTIVE until
they radio it picked up, or until `plannedEnd` plus a 12-hour overrun grace
passes with no pickup call, when it is presumed over and RESOLVED. The
planned end is an estimate crews overrun, so it is never mapped onto the
envelope `expires`.

beginLocation.description: Where the closure starts, verbatim, e.g. "Avery".

district.description: Caltrans district whose feed listed it (3 or 10 here).

endIndefinite.description: True when the window has no planned end.

endLocation.description: Where it ends; equals `beginLocation` for a closure at one spot.

estimatedDelayMinutes.description: Caltrans's delay estimate in minutes. 0 when none or not reported.

lanesClosed.description: Lanes closed, verbatim: "1, RShoulder", "All", "Rt Turn Ln".

plannedEnd.description: Planned end of the window. `null` when `endIndefinite`.

setUpAt.description:
When the crew radioed the closure set up (the 10-97 call). `null` while it
is SCHEDULED.

totalLanes.description: Number of lanes at the site. 0 when not reported.

windowId.description: CWWP2 window id, unique per window.

workType.description: Work being done, e.g. "Drainage Work", "Tree Work".

v1LatLng.description:
LatLng is one WGS 84 point in decimal degrees. Note the order: unlike GeoJSON
coordinates, this is latitude first.

v1Layer.description:
Layer is the event taxonomy. Response values are these UPPERCASE names; the
`layer` query parameter also accepts lowercase slugs (`road_incident`).

Only event layers appear here. The condition layers (`road_segment`,
`chain_control`, `fire_weather`, `message_sign`) are map layers and summary
inputs, never events.

 - LAYER_UNSPECIFIED: Never returned.
 - WILDFIRE: Wildfires: CAL FIRE incidents joined with FIRIS/NIFC perimeters (sources
`calfire`, `firis`). Scoped wider than other layers, so a fire approaching
the region shows up before it arrives.
 - EVACUATION: Evacuation zones under an order, warning, advisory or shelter-in-place,
from Cal OES / Genasys (source `caloes`). Life-safety: see the summary's
`activeEvacuations`.
 - WEATHER_ALERT: National Weather Service watches, warnings and advisories for the region's
forecast zones (source `nws`). No geometry; attached to places by zone.
 - FIRE_WEATHER: Reserved. Fire weather is a condition (`GET /api/v1/conditions`), not an
event layer; no event carries it.
 - EARTHQUAKE: USGS earthquakes of magnitude 2.5 or more in the last 7 days (source `usgs`).
 - ROAD_INCIDENT: CHP traffic incidents (source `chp`, AI-summarized) and Caltrans planned
lane-closure windows (source `caltrans`). Planned windows not yet set up are
SCHEDULED.
 - POWER: 
PG&E electric outages (source `pge`) and Public Safety Power Shutoffs
(source `psps`). Most outages affect one customer and are INFO.
 - GAUGE: Reserved for stream gauges; no events today.
 - AIR_QUALITY: Reserved for air quality; no events today.
 - MESH: MeshCore community radio nodes (source `meshcore`), one event per node.
Ambient INFO state, not a hazard. It dominates an unscoped event query.
 - ANNOUNCEMENT: Reserved for announcements; no events today.
 - BURN_STATUS: One event per tracked county saying whether residential burning is allowed
today (sources `burnline`, `calfire-burn`). Ambient, permanently ACTIVE,
always INFO; its revision history is the record of changes.

v1LayerStats.description: LayerStats is one layer's share of Stats.

v1MeshAdminTelemetry.description:
MeshAdminTelemetry is one reading taken from a node's own admin interface by an
operator-run monitor. It is the node's self-reported view, which is why it
sits beside rather than replaces the gateway-reported `snr`/`rssi`: those are
what a distant listener heard, these are what the node measured.

Gauges are nullable: `null` means the monitor could not read it, which is not
the same as 0 (a 0% battery and an unknown battery must not render alike).
Counters are plain, count since the node's last boot (they reset at a
reboot), and are 64-bit, so they arrive as JSON STRINGS.

batteryPercent.description: Battery charge in percent, 0-100. Nullable. See `batteryPercentSource`.

batteryPercentSource.description:
Whether `batteryPercent` was measured by the node or estimated from
voltage. Empty string when no percentage is reported.

directDups.description: Duplicate direct-routed packets dropped since boot.

floodDups.description: Duplicate flood-routed packets dropped since boot.

humidity.description: Relative humidity in percent. Nullable (most nodes have no sensor).

lastAttemptAt.description:
The monitor's last attempt to read this node, successful or not. Can be
`null` (always `null` on archived samples).

lastRssiDbm.description: RSSI of the last packet the node itself received, in dBm. Nullable.

lastSnrDb.description: SNR of the last packet the node itself received, in dB. Nullable.

lastSuccessAt.description:
The monitor's last successful read of this node. Can be `null` (always
`null` on archived samples).

noiseFloorDbm.description: Radio noise floor in dBm. Nullable.

pressure.description: Barometric pressure in hPa. Nullable (most nodes have no sensor).

reportedAt.description:
When the monitor produced the report. In the archive this is the sample's
own time.

reporterId.description: Which monitor reported it (its registry id, also a row on `/api/v1/sources`).

txQueueLen.description: Packets waiting in the transmit queue. Nullable.

uptimeSeconds.description: Seconds since the node booted. A decrease between samples is a reboot.

v1MeshDetail.description:
MeshDetail is the MESH detail block, for one MeshCore radio node, keyed by its
Ed25519 public key.

Identity, location and reachability changes write a revision. The volatile
signal readings in `telemetry` change constantly without one.

name.description: Name the node advertises. Free text and can include emoji.

nodeType.description:
Node role as advertised. Repeaters and room servers relay traffic;
companions and sensors do not.

publicKey.description:
Full Ed25519 public key, 64 lowercase hex characters. It is also the native
half of the event id (`meshcore:{publicKey}`) and the `node` parameter of
`GET /api/v1/mesh/telemetry`.

reachability.description:
Whether an operator-run monitor can reach this node's admin interface.
MESH_REACHABILITY_UNSPECIFIED for the many nodes no monitor watches. A
change writes a revision, so the history answers "how often is this
repeater down?".

telemetry.description: Signal readings and activity clocks. These change without a new revision.

v1MeshReachability.description:
MeshReachability is an operator monitor's verdict on a node's admin interface,
smoothed so a marginal link does not flap.

 - MESH_REACHABILITY_UNSPECIFIED: No monitor watches this node (most nodes). Says nothing about liveness.
 - REACHABLE: A monitor reached it recently.
 - UNREACHABLE: A monitor has been failing to reach it for longer than its window.

v1MeshTelemetry.description:
MeshTelemetry is a mesh node's volatile signal state and activity clocks. None
of it writes a revision, so history snapshots do not reflect it.

For "is this node up right now", use `lastRelayedAt` (repeaters relay
constantly but advertise only every day or two), then `lastHeardAt`; never
the event's `observedAt`.

admin.description:
Latest reading from an operator-run monitor that logs into the node's admin
interface. `null` for nodes no monitor watches. The full series is at
`GET /api/v1/mesh/telemetry?node={publicKey}`.

gateways.description: Ids of the gateways (observer node keys, uppercase hex) that heard the node.

hopCount.description:
Hops the last-heard advert travelled; 0 means heard directly. Nullable,
like `snr`: `null` is unknown, not zero hops.

lastAdvertAt.description:
Time stamped by the node itself on its last advert (the node's clock, which
can be wrong). `null` if no bridge has heard an advert.

lastHeardAt.description:
When the Grid last received one of this node's own adverts, by our clock
(compare `lastAdvertAt`, the node's clock). Answers "when did the node last
speak". `null` when no advert has been received since activity tracking
began. Filled at read time on current events only; history revisions do not
carry it.

lastRelayedAt.description:
When the Grid last received a packet this node RELAYED, by our clock. A
repeater advertises every day or two but relays constantly, so this is the
clock that says it is up right now. `null` when no relay has been
attributed. Read-time only, like `lastHeardAt`.

A hop is credited only when exactly one relay-capable node fits it, so a
node whose traffic is ambiguous gets no relay time (it reads older than on
other mesh tools). Flood-routed packets of any type credit every hop; a
direct-routed packet's remaining route credits its 2- and 3-byte hops only.
A relay also keeps a known node ACTIVE for a while after it, the way an
advert does; it never creates a node or changes its name or position.

rssi.description:
Received signal strength of the last advert, in dBm, gateway-reported.
Nullable, like `snr`.

snr.description:
Signal-to-noise ratio of the last advert, in dB, as a listening gateway
reported it. Nullable: `null` unless an MQTT bridge heard the advert (then
`lastAdvertAt` is set too).

v1MeshTelemetryArchive.description:
MeshTelemetryArchive is one node's samples over a window, with what a chart
needs in order not to lie about them.

cadenceSeconds.description:
Median gap between samples in the window, in seconds, so a chart knows which
gaps are abnormal enough to break a line on. 64-bit, so a JSON STRING
(`"1831"`). Nullable: `null` with fewer than two samples.

coverage.description:
What the archive holds for this node at all, whatever window was asked
for. A window outside it has no samples because we do not have them, which
is not the same as the node being quiet.

from.description: Window start actually used (after defaults and clamping).

node.description:
The requested node, normalized to the bare lowercase key (no `meshcore:`
prefix).

reboots.description:
Sample times where the node's uptime went backwards, i.e. it rebooted. Every
counter restarts there, so break counter lines at these times. Empty list
when none.

samples.description: Samples in the window, oldest first.

truncated.description:
True when the window held more than the 20,000 samples one response carries;
the series ends early. Narrow the window to see the rest.

v1MeshTelemetryCoverage.description: MeshTelemetryCoverage is the span of the whole archive for one node.

from.description: Oldest archived sample. `null` when the archive holds none.

samples.description: Number of archived samples in total.

to.description: Newest archived sample. `null` when the archive holds none.

reading.description:
The reading. `reading.reportedAt` is the sample's own time; gauges are
nullable exactly as on the live event.

receivedAt.description: When the Grid first stored it.

v1Place.description: Place is a named geography that events attach to.

geometry.description:
The place's shape: a Polygon for counties and areas, a LineString for
corridors, a Point for towns.

kind.description: What kind of place this is.

parentId.description: Id of the containing place (a town's county). Empty string when none.

slug.description:
URL-safe short name, unique across all kinds. Use it in paths and the
`place` parameter.

v1PlaceKind.description:
PlaceKind is the type of a place.

 - PLACE_KIND_UNSPECIFIED: Never returned.
 - AREA: A configured coverage area such as `ebbetts-pass` (the Highway 4 corridor
region). Area places own the scanner feeds and the fire-weather zones.
 - COUNTY: A county, from Census polygons.
 - TOWN: A town, stored as a Point. `places:resolve` matches a town within 3 km of
its point. Events attach to a town only by overlapping polygons (and
wildfires by proximity), never by that radius.
 - EVAC_ZONE: Reserved for evacuation zones as places; none exist today.
 - CORRIDOR: A highway segment, stored as a LineString. Point events within about 1.5 km
of the line attach to it.
 - SITE: Reserved for individual sites; none exist today.

places.description: Places, ordered by kind and then name.

v1PlaceSummary.description:
PlaceSummary is the one-call rollup for a place.

`summary` covers hazards only. Each entry in `domains` covers one subject
area, including the ambient ones (`burn`, `comms`) that the hazard rollup
leaves out.

domains.description:
One block per domain, always in this order: `fire`, `evacuation`,
`weather`, `roads`, `seismic`, `power`, then `burn` (when burn counties are
configured) and `comms` (when the mesh source is enabled). Both are
configured in production.

mode.description:
Overall posture. The rules below are checked in order and the first match
wins.

- `ACTIVE`: an active evacuation at ORDER, WARNING or SHELTER_IN_PLACE; or
  any active EXTREME event; or an active wildfire at SEVERE or above.
- `WATCH`: any active SEVERE event; or an active evacuation ADVISORY; or
  fire weather `elevated` (Fire Weather Watch) or `red-flag` (Red Flag
  Warning) for a place inside a coverage area; or the evacuation source
  UNAVAILABLE (unknown is never quiet); or any layer feeding the
  summary UNAVAILABLE while an active event is MODERATE or above.
- `QUIET`: otherwise. A MODERATE or lower event on its own leaves the
  place QUIET.

Only these inputs can raise it: ACTIVE events on the WILDFIRE,
EVACUATION, WEATHER_ALERT, EARTHQUAKE, ROAD_INCIDENT and POWER layers
(by severity), the fire-weather state, and source health. These never
raise it: SCHEDULED events (a planned closure, a watch or PSPS not yet in
effect), MESH nodes, BURN_STATUS, INFO POWER outages, and every condition
other than fire weather. A CLOSED `road_segment` or a chain control
raises the `roads` domain's `highestSeverity`, not `mode`, so a place can
be QUIET with a closed highway. Show each domain's `status` and
`highestSeverity` alongside `mode`.

sources.description:
Health of the sources behind the summary's layers. Region-wide, not
specific to the place.

v1PowerDetail.description:
PowerDetail is the POWER detail block, for a PG&E outage or a Public Safety
Power Shutoff (PSPS). The envelope `category` says which: `unplanned` and
`planned` outages fill the outage fields; `psps` fills the PSPS fields. The
other group is zero, empty or `null`.

Every PG&E time here is an estimate PG&E often overruns, so none of them is
mapped onto the envelope `expires` or drives the lifecycle.

allClear.description:
PG&E's planned all-clear time. A plan, not proof the shutoff ended: it is
set even while the stage is still Watch. Never use it to decide the power
is back; use `status`.

cause.description:
Raw PG&E cause code, e.g. "PLNND SHUTDOWN", "TREE CONTACT", "EMERG REPAIRS".
Empty string for PSPS.

crewStatus.description:
PG&E crew status, verbatim: "Awaiting T-Man", "T-Man On Site", "Crew On
Site", "No Access", ... Empty string for PSPS.

customersAffected.description:
Estimated customers without power. 0 means PG&E gave no count. Statewide,
the median outage affects one customer.

deEnergizationEnd.description: Planned end of de-energization (an estimate). `null` for outages.

deEnergizationStart.description: Planned start of de-energization. `null` for outages.

estimatedRestoration.description:
PG&E's estimated time of restoration. An estimate that is often missed;
`null` when not given.

eventId.description:
--- PSPS (source `psps`) ---
PG&E PSPS event id. Empty string for outages.

eventName.description: PG&E PSPS event name. Empty string for outages.

medicalBaselineAffected.description:
Medical-baseline customers in the shutoff footprint: people whose medical
equipment depends on grid power. No other feed reports this.

outageId.description:
--- outage (source `pge`) ---
PG&E outage id, the native half of `pge:{id}`. Empty string for PSPS.

stage.description:
PSPS stage: `Watch` (shutoff under consideration, MODERATE) or `Warning`
(shutoff committed, SEVERE). Empty string for outages.

timePeriod.description:
The de-energization time-period slice this event covers. Empty string for
outages.

v1Provenance.description:
Provenance says which upstream published an event. Show `attribution` next to
the data.

attribution.description:
Attribution text to display, e.g. "CAL FIRE / FIRIS / NIFC". Can be an
empty string.

fetchedAt.description: When the Grid fetched the upstream data behind this revision.

sourceId.description: Source registry id; joins to `Source.id` on `/api/v1/sources`.

sourceName.description:
Display name of the publisher, e.g. "CAL FIRE", "NWS Sacramento CA",
"CHP / Caltrans".

sourceUrl.description:
Link to the publisher's page for this item or feed (for evacuations, the
Genasys or county zone viewer). Empty string when none, which today means
CHP incidents, Caltrans lane closures, FIRIS perimeters, NWS alerts and
burn status. Fall back to `Source.homepageUrl` for `sourceId`.

v1RelatedEvent.description: RelatedEvent is one related event and why.

event.description: The related event, without its shape (bbox and centroid only).

reason.description: One plain sentence, e.g. "Cal OES notes name the Ross Fire".
reason.example: Cal OES notes name the Ross Fire

rule.description:
The rule that matched, e.g. `fire-evacuation-named`,
`fire-evacuation-near`, `fire-outage-cause`, `fire-shutoff-near`,
`fire-road-named`, `weather-shutoff`, `weather-outage`, `weather-road`.
New rules may appear; treat unknown names generically.

v1RelatedEventList.description: RelatedEventList is the events related to one event, strongest first.

v1RelationConfidence.description:
RelationConfidence is how strongly a relation is supported.

 - RELATION_CONTEXT: Coincidence in time and place worth showing as context; no link claimed
(an outage inside a High Wind Warning's area).
 - RELATION_LOW: Plausible from time and place alone (a shutoff near a burning fire).
 - RELATION_MEDIUM: Time and place plus a corroborating fact (PG&E lists the cause as fire),
or the nearest fire to an evacuation zone issued soon after it started.
 - RELATION_HIGH: A source names the other event (Cal OES notes name the fire).

v1ResolvePlaceResponse.description: ResolvePlaceResponse lists the places containing a point.

places.description:
Containing places, most specific first. Empty when the point is outside
every place.

v1ResolveQuery.description: ResolveQuery echoes the point that was resolved.

lat.description: Latitude used for the lookup (the geocoded point for an address).

matchedAddress.description:
The address the geocoder matched, normalized. Empty string for a lat/lng
query.

v1RoadHistory.description: RoadHistory is one segment's samples over a window.

v1RoadIncidentDetail.description:
RoadIncidentDetail is the ROAD_INCIDENT detail block, for a CHP incident or a
Caltrans lane-closure window. The incident type is the envelope `category`,
the location is `areaLabel`, and the short line is `headline`.

closure.description:
The Caltrans closure window, for source `caltrans` only; `null` for CHP
incidents.

duration.description: AI-estimated duration (CHP incidents only). Empty string when not assessed.

impact.description:
AI-assessed traffic impact (CHP incidents only); it drives `severity`.
Empty string for Caltrans closures and when not yet assessed.

log.description:
CHP's numbered incident log, oldest first: what dispatch recorded and
when. Parsed from the feed's structure, not AI. The same lines are in
`description` verbatim. Empty for Caltrans closures and when CHP has
logged nothing. A new line is a new revision.

logNumber.description: CHP log number for an incident; for a Caltrans closure, its closure id.

metadata.description:
Free-form extras from the AI analysis, string to string (keys such as
`incident_type`, `lanes_blocked`, `injuries`). Keys vary; treat as display
only. Empty object when none.

v1RoadSample.description: RoadSample is a segment at one roads refresh.

congestion.description: CLEAR, LIGHT, MODERATE, HEAVY or SEVERE.

durationMinutes.description: Travel time and delay, minutes. `null` when that refresh had none.

status.description: OPEN, RESTRICTED, CLOSED or MAINTENANCE, as on the road_segment layer.

v1Scanner.description: Scanner is one Broadcastify audio feed.

v1Severity.description:
Severity is the unified 5-level scale shared by every layer: how urgently the
public should respond, not physical magnitude. The enum number is the rank
(`severityRank`, 0-4), for sorting and colour ramps.

How each layer is graded. WILDFIRE: the worse of a containment floor (under
50% contained SEVERE, 50-99% MODERATE, 100% MINOR) and size (1,000+ acres
under 50% contained EXTREME, 100+ acres SEVERE). EVACUATION: ORDER EXTREME,
WARNING and SHELTER_IN_PLACE SEVERE, ADVISORY MODERATE. WEATHER_ALERT: the NWS
severity (Extreme..Minor) one-to-one, otherwise INFO. EARTHQUAKE: M5+ SEVERE,
M4+ MODERATE, M2.5+ MINOR. ROAD_INCIDENT: a CHP incident by its AI-assessed
impact (severe SEVERE, moderate MODERATE, light MINOR, none INFO); a Caltrans
closure by its structure (full closure SEVERE, a travel lane or one-way
traffic MODERATE, shoulder only MINOR). POWER: 1,000+ customers SEVERE, 100+
MODERATE, 10+ MINOR, fewer INFO, unknown count MINOR, planned outages one rank
lower; PSPS Warning SEVERE, Watch MODERATE. MESH and BURN_STATUS: always INFO.
Condition layers on the map: road segment CLOSED SEVERE, restricted or heavy
congestion MODERATE; chain control R3 SEVERE, R2 MODERATE, R1 MINOR, road
closed MINOR; fire weather red-flag SEVERE, elevated MODERATE.

 - INFO: Rank 0. Informational: ambient state, single-customer outages, small quakes,
clear roads. Also the default when a source gives no grade.
 - MINOR: Rank 1. Minor impact.
 - MODERATE: Rank 2. Moderate impact; worth attention.
 - SEVERE: Rank 3. Severe; act or prepare now.
 - EXTREME: Rank 4. Extreme; life-safety (evacuation orders, large uncontained fires).

v1Source.description:
Source is one row of the source registry, with its health.

Two kinds of row, told apart by `kind`: a FEED is an upstream the Grid
fetches on a schedule, and its id is what events carry in
`provenance.sourceId`. A REPORTER is an operator-run monitor that pushes data
to the Grid (`alanpi`, `relay`, `burn-line`); its row carries health only and
no event names it as its source.

To judge health, read `status`. It is rewritten at every attempt, so as a
second check against the Grid itself stalling, treat a row as suspect when
`lastAttemptAt` is older than `staleAfterSeconds`. Do not compare
`lastAttemptAt` with `pollIntervalSeconds`: that misfires for reporters.

Not every source id that appears in the API has a row. The live condition
layers fetch on request, outside the scheduler that writes this registry, so
`google` (the `road_segment` layer's travel times) has no row, and the
`caltrans` and `nws` rows describe the scheduled lane-closure and alert
polls, not the live `chain_control`, `message_sign`, `road_segment` and
`fire_weather` fetches. For those layers read the map layer's
`metadata.sourceStatus` or the summary domain's `status`.

expireAfterSeconds.description:
For sources whose silence proves nothing (NWS, FIRIS, MeshCore): how long,
in seconds, an event may go unseen before it is EXPIRED. 0 means the source
never auto-expires; its events are RESOLVED when a good poll stops listing
them.

homepageUrl.description:
Public page for the upstream. Use it as the fallback link for an event
whose `canonicalUrl` and `provenance.sourceUrl` are empty (join on
`provenance.sourceId`). Empty string for REPORTER rows, and for a feed with
no public page.

id.description: Registry id; `Provenance.sourceId` on events joins to it (FEED rows only).

kind.description: Whether this row is a scheduled feed or a push reporter.

lastAttemptAt.description:
When the row was last evaluated, successfully or not. `null` if never.
`status` is rewritten at each attempt, so if this is older than
`staleAfterSeconds`, the Grid itself has stopped checking: treat the
source as STALE whatever `status` says.

lastError.description: The last attempt's error text. Empty string after a success.

lastSuccessAt.description:
When an attempt last succeeded. `null` if never. For a REPORTER this is the
last check that found it reporting on time, not the time of its last
report (`lastError` names that once it goes quiet).

pollIntervalSeconds.description:
How often, in seconds, the Grid re-evaluates this row. For a FEED that is
its poll interval. For a REPORTER it is the cadence of the Grid's check on
the reporter, not how often the reporter reports.

staleAfterSeconds.description:
For a FEED: seconds after the last success during which a failing source
still reads STALE rather than UNAVAILABLE (default three poll intervals).
For a REPORTER: how long it may go without reporting before it stops
reading OK (it then reads STALE for this long again, then UNAVAILABLE).

status.description:
Health of this source. This is the field to judge it by; see the message
description.

v1SourceKind.description:
SourceKind says what a source registry row describes.

 - SOURCE_KIND_UNSPECIFIED: Never returned.
 - FEED: An upstream feed the Grid fetches on a schedule (CAL FIRE, NWS, PG&E, ...).
Events name it in `provenance.sourceId`.
 - REPORTER: An operator-run monitor that pushes to the Grid's ingest endpoint. Health
only: no event carries its id, and `homepageUrl` is empty.

sources.description: Every source, ordered by id, including the health-only push-reporter rows.

v1SourceStatus.description:
SourceStatus is a source's health. The same three values appear as strings in
the summary's domains and sidecar, on `/api/v1/cameras`, and on the map
layers' `metadata.sourceStatus`.

 - SOURCE_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED: Not polled yet since the registry row was created. Treat as UNAVAILABLE.
 - OK: The last attempt succeeded.
 - STALE: The last attempt failed, but the last success is within
`staleAfterSeconds`; what is served is last-good data.
 - UNAVAILABLE: Failing beyond `staleAfterSeconds`, or never succeeded. Nothing current can
be vouched for: render "unknown", never "none".

v1Stats.description: Stats is what the Grid has recorded, overall and per layer.

computedAt.description: When these totals were computed (they are cached for up to five minutes).

events.title:
Events ever stored, in every status.
(int32 so JSON carries a number, not a string.)

layers.description:
Per-layer totals, largest event count first. Layers with no events are
left out.

place.description: The resolved place id, or empty for every event.

revisions.description: Revisions recorded across those events (each event's `revision` summed).

since.description:
When the earliest of those events was first stored. Null when there are
none.

sources.description: Distinct sources those events came from.

v1SummaryDomain.description:
SummaryDomain is one subject area's status for the place.

Domain inputs: `fire` = WILDFIRE events + the fire_weather condition;
`evacuation` = EVACUATION; `weather` = WEATHER_ALERT; `roads` = ROAD_INCIDENT
events (not SCHEDULED roadwork) + the chain_control and road_segment
conditions; `seismic` = EARTHQUAKE; `power` = POWER (including INFO
outages); `burn` = BURN_STATUS; `comms` = MESH. A domain counts every one of
its ACTIVE and SCHEDULED events at any severity, but a condition only when it
is above INFO (an open road or normal fire weather is not "active").

activeCount.description:
Number of counted items (events plus above-INFO conditions). It can be
non-zero while `summary.totalActive` is 0: `comms` counts mesh nodes,
`burn` counts burn status, and `power` counts INFO outages.

headlines.description:
Up to three counted items, most severe first (events before conditions on
ties). An item is an event OR a condition-layer feature; check `kind`.

highestSeverity.description: Highest severity among the domain's counted items; `INFO` when none.

status.description:
The WORST source status across the domain's layers, so partial data never
presents as complete. A failing source with stored events reads STALE.

v1SummaryDomainHeadline.description:
SummaryDomainHeadline is one item in a domain's headline list: an event, or a
live condition-layer feature (a closed road segment, a chain control, a fire
weather banner). Use `kind` to tell them apart before following `id`.

id.description:
The item's id. For `kind: EVENT` an event id, fetchable at
`GET /api/v1/events/{id}`. For `kind: CONDITION` a map-feature id
(`road:{segment}`, `cc:{route}:{level}`, `fw:region`): it is NOT an event and
`GET /api/v1/events/{id}` returns 404. Find it as `properties.id` in the
place's `{layer}.geojson` map layer (the layer slug is `layer` lowercased).
A chain requirement is one headline per stretch of highway
(`cc:hwy4:r2`, "Hwy 4 chains required, Poison Springs to Mount Reba Road
(R2)"), not one per Caltrans sign; a pass closure gate keeps
`cc:{district}-{message id}`.
A seasonal closure past a road segment's end has the id
`road:{segment}:beyond-{n}`: the part before `:beyond-` is the segment
feature's id and `n` is the index into its `road.beyond`. It is not a
road id: `GET /api/v1/roads/{road}/history` returns 404 for it.

kind.description:
`EVENT` when `id` is a stored event, `CONDITION` when it is a live
condition-layer map feature with no event record.

layer.description:
The item's layer, UPPERCASE. For an event, its `Event.layer`. For a
condition, the condition layer (`ROAD_SEGMENT`, `CHAIN_CONTROL`,
`FIRE_WEATHER`); lowercase it for the `.geojson` map-layer path.

v1SummarySourceHealth.description: SummarySourceHealth is one source registry row behind the summary's layers.

lastSuccessAt.description: When the source last polled successfully. `null` if never.

status.description: The source's health. A source never polled reads `UNAVAILABLE`.

v1SummaryStats.description:
SummaryStats is the place's hazard rollup.

It counts the place's ACTIVE and SCHEDULED events except four carve-outs:
MESH nodes and BURN_STATUS (ambient state, shown in their own domains), POWER
outages at INFO (single-customer service calls), and SCHEDULED road closures
(planned roadwork). A SCHEDULED weather watch or PSPS still counts. Condition
layers never count here.

activeEvacuations.description:
ACTIVE evacuation zones attached to the place. NULLABLE: `null` when the
evacuation source is UNAVAILABLE with nothing stored (unknown: render
"unknown, check Genasys", never "none"). `0` means a healthy fetch found no
active zone ("no active evacuations reported", not a guarantee). Never
coerce `null` to 0.

evacuationSourceUrl.description:
The authoritative evacuation viewer (Genasys Protect), the same link as
the `evacuation` map layer's `metadata.sourceUrl`. Always set, whatever
`evacuationStatus` says: it is where to send people when the count is
`null` ("unknown, check Genasys") and the place to confirm a 0 or an N.
For one zone's own page use the event's `provenance.sourceUrl`.

evacuationStatus.description:
Health of the evacuation source as served: `OK`, `STALE` (source failing
but stored zones are served; the count is last-good) or `UNAVAILABLE`
(then `activeEvacuations` is `null`).

highestSeverity.description: Highest severity among the counted events; `INFO` when there are none.

severityCounts.description:
Count of counted events per severity name (`INFO` .. `EXTREME`). A severity
with no events is absent rather than 0.

topEvents.description:
Up to five counted events, most severe first, then most recently observed.
Every id here is an event (`GET /api/v1/events/{id}`).

totalActive.description: Number of counted events (ACTIVE and SCHEDULED, after the carve-outs).

v1SummaryTopEvent.description: SummaryTopEvent is one of the place's most urgent hazard events.

layer.description:
The event's layer as the UPPERCASE enum name, the same value as
`Event.layer`. Never MESH or BURN_STATUS (excluded from the rollup).

v1TimelineClock.description:
TimelineClock says whose time an entry is.

 - TIMELINE_CLOCK_SOURCE: A time the upstream source stated.
 - TIMELINE_CLOCK_GRID: When the Grid recorded something (a revision's ingest time).

v1TimelineEntry.description: TimelineEntry is one moment in an event's timeline.

detail.description: Supporting text: who said it, a log line number, what it was before.

field.description:
For CHANGED and STATUS: the field (`status`, `severity`, `acres`,
`containment`, `level`, `customersAffected`) and its values before and
after, as displayed.

label.description:
A short label in plain words, e.g. "Reported", "Set up on the road",
"Resolved", "Containment 40%".

revision.description: For GRID entries, the revision that recorded it; 0 otherwise.

v1TimelineKind.description:
TimelineKind is what an entry marks.

 - TIMELINE_BEGINS: SOURCE. When it began or was reported: CHP's report time, a fire's start,
an outage's start, an earthquake's origin time, when an alert or
evacuation takes effect.
 - TIMELINE_LOG: SOURCE. One line of the source's own log (CHP). `detail` is the line
number.
 - TIMELINE_PLANNED_START: SOURCE. A planned start (lane closure window, PSPS de-energization).
 - TIMELINE_SET_UP: SOURCE. The crew reported the closure set up on the road.
 - TIMELINE_PLANNED_END: SOURCE. A planned end.
 - TIMELINE_ENDS: SOURCE. When the source says it ends or expires (an alert's end, an
evacuation's expiry).
 - TIMELINE_ESTIMATE: SOURCE. An estimate, e.g. PG&E's estimated restoration. Estimates are
routinely revised.
 - TIMELINE_ALL_CLEAR: SOURCE. PG&E's all-clear for a shutoff.
 - TIMELINE_ACTIVITY: SOURCE. Latest activity of a mesh node: last advert, last heard, last
relayed, a monitor's last read or attempt.
 - TIMELINE_FIRST_RECORDED: GRID. The Grid first stored the event (revision 1).
 - TIMELINE_STATUS: GRID. The event's status changed; `before` and `after` are statuses.
 - TIMELINE_CHANGED: GRID. A tracked value changed between revisions; `field` names it.

v1WeatherAlertDetail.description:
WeatherAlertDetail is the WEATHER_ALERT detail block, for one NWS product.

It carries only fields the envelope lacks: the NWS event name is the
envelope `category`, and the issuing office is `provenance.sourceName`.

areaDesc.description: NWS free-text list of the affected zones.

instruction.description: NWS recommended actions, verbatim, with newlines. Empty string when none.

nwsSeverity.description: NWS's own severity word, distinct from the unified `severity` it maps to.

replacedByEventId.description:
Grid event id of the alert that replaced this one, e.g. "wx:urn:oid:...".
Mirrors NWS's own `replacedBy` / the CAP `references` of the newer message.
Set only when this alert was retired (status RESOLVED) because a newer
alert referenced it, and from that revision on; empty otherwise, including
for an alert that was cancelled or simply lapsed.

zones.description: NWS forecast zone codes the alert covers, e.g. "CAZ138".

v1WeatherConditions.description:
WeatherConditions is current weather at one location, from OpenWeatherMap.
Whole numbers, metric units. A value that could not be read is 0.

observedAt.description:
When this town's reading was taken (our fetch time). When a town's
fetch fails its previous reading is kept, so this can be older than
`Conditions.lastUpdated`; past 1.5x the refresh interval
`weatherStatus` is STALE. Null when unknown.

weatherIcon.description:
OpenWeatherMap icon code; the image is
`https://openweathermap.org/img/wn/{icon}@2x.png`.

windDirectionDegrees.description: Direction the wind blows FROM, degrees clockwise from north.

v1WeatherForecast.description:
WeatherForecast is a location's short-range forecast: the hourly NWS gridpoint
series (wind, gust, humidity, temperature) plus an at-a-glance summary.
Informational only: it never implies a fire-weather warning (issued products
are in `fireWeather`).

daily.description:
The 7-day forecast in NWS's named 12-hour periods, in time order. Empty
when that product could not be fetched.

gridElevationMeters.description:
Elevation of the NWS grid cell this forecast is for, metres. It can
differ from the town's own elevation by hundreds of metres. `null` when
NWS gave none.

issuedAt.description: When NWS last updated the grid. Can be `null`.

minHumidityPercent.description: Lowest relative humidity over the horizon, percent. 0 when NWS gave none.

peakWindGustAt.description: When that peak gust is forecast. Can be `null`.

peakWindGustKmh.description: Highest wind gust over the horizon, km/h.

source.description: Data source and NWS grid cell.

elevationMeters.description:
Ground elevation at the location, metres (USGS 3DEP). `null` when not
configured.

zone.description: The NWS public forecast zone containing it, e.g. `CAZ138`.

v1WildfireDetail.description: WildfireDetail is the WILDFIRE detail block.

acres.description:
Burned area in acres: CAL FIRE's figure, or the FIRIS perimeter's area when
only a perimeter is known. Fractional.

cause.description: Cause as reported. Empty string when unknown.

containment.description: Percent contained, 0-100. 0 also when unknown (perimeter-only fires).

county.description: County named by CAL FIRE. Empty string for perimeter-only fires.

hasPerimeter.description:
True when `geometry` is a FIRIS perimeter polygon; false when it is CAL
FIRE's single origin point.

ingestBearer.description:
A per-reporter token issued by the operators (256-bit random, shown once).
Only its SHA-256 lives server-side. Identity comes from the token alone:
any reporter id in the body is ignored.
